checks: The three edge inequalities follow from the vertices of the bounded triangle. Independent integer enumeration of the complete box [1,4]×[−2,3] gives exactly the nine displayed bases, and substitution gives all nine roof values. The two roof inequalities and the nonnegative simplex coordinates describe a convex compact polytope. The positive roof and positive-area triangle give full ambient dimension, including R=0.

The scale is positive and strictly orders volumes as the roof height orders them. Replaying parity partition and squared norms yields roots 0,1,2,5, with exactly the two stated maximum ties. The five unique nonroot midpoint arrows terminate. Their scale identities include the common offset R on both sides, so the homothetic Minkowski set equalities hold at every d≥1.

The standard simplex has volume 1/d! and centroid 1_d/(d+1), making each graph atom exactly the actual scaled-fiber centroid with its original volume. The affine height extraction maps all the atoms to the displayed three-coordinate census. Every displayed graph cap pulls back to a proper closed ambient halfspace, with its listed index on the boundary.

Recomputed all 81 normal scores with integers and obtained exactly the nine listed closed traces, each of size at most two. Each atomic weight is at most a in units of 1/d!, giving an upper bound for every graph mark. At G1 the exact graph midpoint identity forces every closed containing halfspace to contain G0 or G4, including equality cases. All three weights equal a, and the row for G1 attains 2a. This matches the upper bound against all normals.

The nine scale powers sum to the stated denominator. At d=1 the roof values sum to 112. The inequality for R>0 follows from 8(R+14)<9R+112. Exact subtraction gives the gap 3/172 at R=21. Dividing by R^d gives the limit 2/9. At R=63d−7 the ratio is at most the finite geometric sum below 9/8, so twice the maximum weight is strictly below one quarter of even nine times the minimum weight.

Source 90f577d65c14ec9f §§1–5 proves exactly this graph obstruction. The separate continuous-volume compensation in §6 is outside the exact claim. overlap.comparison: This example satisfies its homothetic zero-forest hypotheses after centering the common simplex and writing the actual centroids as translations. Its roof-face covering and affine-centroid conclusions on each root patch are compatible with the failure of a global graph quarter-mass bound.
That quarter-mass bound assumes the specified eight bases and exact edge census. This construction has nine bases and different root partners, so the finite ray-exchange proof does not apply.

Its graph Helly conclusion assumes every same-parity pair has its graph midpoint. Here the equal-parity bases p3 and p7 have base midpoint p5, but heights 14 and 10 average to 12 rather than t5=14. The forest edges therefore do not supply its full graph hypothesis.

Its asymptotically shallow weighted graph uses the selected even fibers of a moving-ball family. It does not require an exact canonical zero-slack forest on all occupied integer fibers or determine the current exact maximum.
